topics.topic: Refusal/error classification when a referenced flow or flow version is missing/invalid (including existence vs activation distinctions)
questions: If the requested flow version does not exist (or does not belong to the named flow), is this treated as an unknown reference refusal before proof, or as an unproven/proof failure?
What is the required refusal when the referenced flow or flow version does not exist at all (cannot be proven)?
If both are effectively false from caller perspective (unknown flow id vs known flow without active version), which exact refusal reason must be emitted and traced?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A refuses a missing flow/flow-version as an unknown reference before proof/start checks; behavior B treats it as an unproven/proof failure (or as the same refusal as "no active version"). The owner or agent caller notices different refusal reason/details and trace meaning.
judgement.why: The rules do not pin one required refusal classification for missing flow/version references at activation, so careful implementations can return different observable failures.

topics.topic: Scope of authority/approval gating by operation class (including whether reads ever wait/refuse)
questions: Does this 'waits for approval' branch apply to all operation classes, or only to classes that require runtime approval (`state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`, plus resend-after-`not_applied` cases)?
When reaching a `read` operation element, is the authority step a no-op (never waits), or must implementation still run generic authority logic that could wait/refuse?

quotes: `draft-write` nodes ask nothing at run time: K-08 lists the classes that stop for approval, and `draft-write` is not one; its authority is the owner's activation of the flow version (A06).
Before sending a `state-transition`, `external-effect` or `destructive` node, the kernel needs one of: an approved, unused EffectApproval M24 of that run, node and element whose
then, for an operation other than `read`, one store call writes the EffectAttempt `in_flight`, naming the approval or grant it uses;
judgement.why: These passages restrict runtime approval waits to the listed effect classes (plus explicit resend cases) and exclude `read` from that approval/effect-attempt path.

topics.topic: Allowed sources for map_over ports (edge from many output only vs constants/non-edge sources)
questions: Must a `map_over` port be fed by an incoming edge from a `many` output, or may it be supplied by a flow constant/list (or another non-edge source)?

topics.topic: Exact event boundary for batching nodes that become non-executable together during advancement writes
questions: What exact event defines the set of nodes that 'become non-executable together' for one write batch during advancement?

topics.topic: How to compute disclosure-proof propagation across guarded/branching paths (path-sensitive vs conservative)
questions: How exactly is "class that can reach" computed across branching/guards (especially mutually exclusive guarded edges): path-sensitive per guard outcome, or conservative max over all possible incoming paths?

topics.topic: Precedence/timing of refusal reasons when manifest digest drift and other binding mismatches coexist
questions: If the manifest digest changed and another rule-5 mismatch is also present, which refusal reason must be returned, and at what point is digest comparison evaluated?

topics.topic: Restart recovery markings for in-flight attempts when authority kind is standing grant or flow activation (not approval)
questions: During restart recovery of `in_flight` attempts, what must be marked when authority was a standing grant or flow activation rather than an approval?

topics.topic: Whether functions may access sandbox filesystem or must remain strictly pure I/O
questions: Are function implementations allowed to read/write files in the sandbox exchange directory, or must all filesystem access be refused to keep functions purely input/output only?
